provenance.title: QUANTUM DIMENSIONS AND THEIR NON-ARCHIMEDEAN DEGENERATIONS
provenance.authors: URI ONN AND JASPER V. STOKMAN

candidates.statement: In each case there is a natural explicit labeling of the irreducible $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{F}}$-spherical $\mathcal{K}_{\mathbb{F}}$-representations $V_\lambda^{\mathbb{F}}$ by partitions $\lambda\in\Lambda_n$ which we shall describe in detail.

Using the identification of right $\mathbb{C}_q(\mathcal{K})$-comodules and left $\mathcal{U}_q$-modules, the subspace of $\mathbb{C}_q(\mathcal{M})$-invariant elements in $V$ coincides with the subspace of $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{m}^{\mathbb{C}})$-invariant elements in $V$, $$V^{\mathbb{C}_q(\mathcal{M})}=\{v\in V \,\, | \,\, Xv=\epsilon(X)v\quad \forall X\in \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{m}^{\mathbb{C}}) \}.$$ In translating the general [CQG ]{.sans-serif}algebra theory from right $\mathbb{C}_q(\mathcal{K})$-modules to left $\mathcal{U}_q$-representations, we shall refer to $\mathbb{C}_q(\mathcal{K})$-spherical representations as $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{m}^{\mathbb{C}})$-spherical representations.

Similarly as for the Koornwinder polynomials and the multivariable little $q$-Jacobi polynomials, the multivariable big $q$-Jacobi polynomials can be characterized by a second-order difference equation they should satisfy, or in terms of suitable orthogonality properties, see [@S0].
